video.title: The High-Paying Remote Skill Nobody Talks About!

summary: Side Hustle Show host Nick Loper interviews Hermela, a former college advisor who pivoted into Salesforce via a free 12-week bootcamp, Trailhead and heavy LinkedIn networking, landing three offers in three months before certifying. Her salary went from ~$53k to $72k remote, then a $105k offer she negotiated to 24 hours a week; she then built freelance managed-service retainers for mission-driven organisations at typical $125-$150/hour rates, plus subcontracting. Key takeaway: pivot to adjacent skills, network directly with decision makers, and favour recurring retainers.

tactics.name: LinkedIn informational-interview outreach
steps: Target peers and hiring managers at organisations in your former industry
Always end with an ask for a 15-30 minute conversation

quote.text: I always leave with, hey, would you be open to a 15 minute conversation or a 30 minute conversation?
quote.speaker: Hermela

tactics.name: Scope a minimum monthly retainer
steps: During sales, scope recurring work together
Set a fixed monthly hours minimum they really need

quote.text: I already know the clients you're going after because I was that client
quote.speaker: Hermela

tactics.name: Negotiate reduced hours
steps: Ask to reduce to 24 hours with pro-rated pay
Use freed days to build freelance clients

warnings.warning: Salary progression in institutions can be capped by budgets and waiting for retirements.

warnings.warning: Project-only work is feast or famine; prefer recurring managed services.
The Salesforce market is more crowded and starting salaries lower than a few years ago.

quote.text: it's a little bit more crowded than when I transitioned
quote.speaker: Hermela

warnings.warning: Blind job applications get filtered out; none of her offers came from them.

lessons.lesson: Mind the gap: keep expenses low and raise income to invest the difference.
Pivot to adjacent skills, translating existing experience (industry knowledge, soft skills).

quote.text: focus on what you have, especially if you're mid-career, you're not starting over from scratch
quote.speaker: Hermela

lessons.lesson: Networking beats applying; offers came before certification.
Treat your day job as your largest client; use freed time to win more.
Recurring retainers weather-proof a consulting business.
Business analysis (translating problems into requirements) gains value with AI.

quote.text: you still need to translate the business problem into technical requirements
quote.speaker: Hermela

lessons.lesson: Learn from someone who has done it (courses) to shortcut setup.
Coast FI: front-load investing so you can work less later.
